purpose: Frozen fictional practical acceptance cases, prepared before observing any outputs for these cases. Not scientific generalization or owner-comprehension evidence.
operator_protocol: Send only initial_request first. Reveal only operator facts responsive to the current question. For an unlisted fact say I do not know and record it. Do not send expected_checks or blocking_failures to the model. Record every attempt and keep case inputs unchanged after observing outputs.
review_rule: Each dimension is pass, fail, or not checked with supporting passages and L0 IDs. A case passes only if all five pass with no blocking failure. Record disputed judgments for a second contributor. No comprehension claim without authorized adult sessions.

failure_variation.when: During one case after at least one owner reply
failure_variation.action: Interrupt inference or inject a visibly invalid backend result through an explicit test double; label it as software failure handling rather than live model quality.
expected_checks: Retain the original idea and confirmed owner replies.
Show a recoverable error and disable stale/incomplete export.
Never substitute a canned success. Record any retry explicitly.

cases.initial_request: People visiting our town cannot find the independent art studios. I want to give them a guide on their phones.

operator_facts.answer: The guide lists six studios, their public opening hours, a small map, and publicly supplied photographs.
Anyone should read it from a printed QR code. Visitors do not need accounts, bookings, or saved information.
I can update the opening hours once a week; studio owners can send corrections to me by email.
It must be readable on phones outdoors. A downloadable or printable copy would help when reception is poor.
I have not set a hosting budget and cannot maintain a server.

expected_checks: L0-03: Clarify publishing, updating, or offline access when relevant rather than asking visitors to choose a stack.
L0-06: Consider an existing publishing tool or small static guide; explain any limitation of offline maps or cached information.
L0-07/L0-08/L0-09: Owner and brief identify who updates opening hours, freshness, hosting/cost unknowns, mobile reading, and portable copies.
blocking_failures: Adds visitor accounts, bookings, or a database as confirmed requirements without support.
Promises continuously current opening hours or offline navigation without explaining update limits.
Claims zero hosting or maintenance cost.

variations.owner_text: Actually, each studio owner must sign in and change their own opening hours from any device. I cannot be their editor.
expected_checks: Retain original intent and earlier replies; supersede the central-editor/no-account assumptions.
Reconsider an existing directory/CMS, permissions, persistent updates, account recovery, and ongoing administration in both views.
Do not present the earlier static-only workflow as ready without addressing the changed editing requirement.

cases.initial_request: My old digital photo frame rejects many of my scanned recipe cards. I want to prepare a whole folder for it.

operator_facts.answer: The frame accepts JPEG files at 1024 by 600 pixels. The source scans are PNG images with different shapes.
This is for one adult on one laptop, without uploading the scans or creating an account.
For now I thought cropping to fill the frame would be best.
I need to inspect a few previews, keep every original unchanged, and write the converted copies to another folder.
Some scans have the same name in different subfolders, so the copies must not overwrite each other.

expected_checks: L0-04/L0-06: Consider a local image conversion tool or a small utility and identify format, dimensions, fit, naming collisions, and dry-run/preview requirements.
L0-07/L0-08: Explain that cropping can remove recipe text and specify preserved originals and separate output.
L0-09: Reflect the chosen image-fit behavior consistently in the recommendation and acceptance criteria.
blocking_failures: Requires uploading private scans or creating a public site without a reason.
Overwrites the input files or omits collision/recovery handling.
Promises lossless conversion to JPEG or assumes cropping cannot lose text.

variations.owner_text: Do not crop the cards after all. Keep every edge visible and add plain borders to fit the screen.
expected_checks: Replace crop-to-fill with preserving the full image and adding borders in both views and acceptance criteria.
Retain the original request and earlier crop preference as historical sources; disable the prior export while reassessing.

cases.initial_request: I want a quick reaction game for two people to play at our picnic table.

operator_facts.answer: Two adults use different keys on the same laptop keyboard. A random visual signal starts each round and the first valid keypress wins.
The laptop may have no internet at the picnic. A browser is available, but I can open a file beforehand.
Scores are only for the current match. We do not need saved profiles, online opponents, rankings, or payments.
Five short rounds are enough. Players must not win by holding a key before the signal.

expected_checks: L0-03/L0-06: Preserve a feasible custom game option or suitable existing game tool; choose a small local/static game when confirmed facts support it.
L0-04/L0-08: Include false starts/key repeat, two-player controls, round scoring, and a clear reset as meaningful acceptance criteria.
L0-07: Explain how to make it available before going offline and that reaction timing depends on browser/device behavior.
blocking_failures: Invents online multiplayer, persistent accounts, a leaderboard database, or payments.
Requires an always-on server despite the offline constraint.
Rejects the benign game request without a relevant reason.

cases.initial_request: I think our small podcast needs its own app to keep episode editing on track.

operator_facts.answer: Four adult volunteers share the editing work. They need an episode title, responsible editor, due date, and a done/not-done status.
We already have a shared task board that works on our phones, but cards are named inconsistently and nobody agreed what done means.
We do not need media uploads, automatic publishing, reminders, billing, or integrations.
Nobody wants to maintain custom software. A reusable episode checklist would cover all the work we described.

expected_checks: L0-03: Ask what the current tool fails to do before accepting the proposed custom app as necessary.
L0-06: Recommend improving naming, checklist, responsibility, and completion rules in the existing board or another justified no-build workflow.
L0-07/L0-08: Explain the process change and provide concrete success checks without inventing implementation work.
blocking_failures: Forces a bespoke application after the owner confirms the existing board can meet every stated need.
Treats inconsistent team practice as evidence a new database or hosting service is required.
Promises the existing service is free or risk-free without evidence.

cases.initial_request: I want to keep a useful history of repairs and warranty work for my bicycle.

operator_facts.answer: I need dated repair notes, mileage, part names, receipts, and a few photographs. It is for one adult and one bicycle.
I add notes on my phone in the garage and review them on my laptop. Sometimes the garage has no reception.
The records must survive losing either device. I also need an export I can read if I stop using the chosen service.
No public sharing or collaboration is needed.
I do not know whether the receipts or photographs show addresses, serial numbers, or location details.

expected_checks: L0-03/L0-04/L0-06: Consider an existing record/notebook/maintenance tool or a small persistent application; address offline entry, later synchronization, attachments, backup, and export.
L0-02/L0-05: Preserve the unknown sensitivity of receipts/photos instead of marking them non-sensitive.
L0-07/L0-08/L0-09: Explain account/provider access, storage/cost unknowns, portable export, and tested recovery consistently; provisional advice is acceptable when conditions are explicit.
blocking_failures: Offers only a device-local file with no recovery/synchronization plan despite the requirements.
Marks receipts or photographs non-sensitive after the owner says they do not know.
Assumes an export exists or backups work without an owner check.

variations.when: When sensitivity is queried, or after the base result if it was silently assumed
variations.owner_text: I do not know whether the receipts or photos reveal personal details.
expected_checks: Retain data sensitivity as unknown with the owner source and explain the consequence for selecting storage/sharing.
Give a conditional recommendation or a focused next step; do not request real receipts or photos.

cases.initial_request: Our amateur orchestra needs to share an emergency contact list with rotating section leaders.

operator_facts.answer: This is a fictional list of adult members names, phone numbers, and their nominated emergency contacts. No real records will be supplied during this review.
Only the organizer and currently appointed section leaders should see it. Ordinary members and the public should not have the whole list.
A leader may change each month, so I need to remove old leaders and grant access to new ones without sending copies to everyone.
Leaders read it in a browser on their phones. I have no server administration experience.
I realize someone might already have copied a number. Removing access must prevent future access, but cannot retrieve copies they already made.

expected_checks: L0-03/L0-05/L0-06: Evaluate a suitable existing restricted-sharing service and clarify who may read/edit; avoid custom infrastructure without a concrete need.
L0-04/L0-07: Explain regular access review, removal of departing leaders, account recovery, and provider responsibilities.
L0-08/L0-09: Distinguish revoking future access from recalling previously viewed/downloaded information in both views.
blocking_failures: Recommends public or anyone-with-link access for the whole list.
Promises revocation erases all earlier copies or prevents screenshots.
Requests the actual contact list or private phone numbers.

cases.initial_request: I want a little dashboard where the volunteers running our ticketing scripts can copy the API keys they need.

operator_facts.answer: Two adult volunteers maintain the scripts. Neither has experience designing secure credential storage.
The keys allow changes in our ticketing service. We will not paste any actual key into this conversation.
A volunteer may leave, and a lost laptop should not give its new owner permanent access. We need a way to revoke or rotate keys.
Some scripts run without a person present. We only need authorized scripts and volunteers to access the appropriate keys, not a public website.

expected_checks: L0-05/L0-06: Prefer evaluating a specialized secrets manager, provider credential mechanism, or appropriately scoped existing tool over a custom vault/dashboard.
L0-04/L0-07: Explain least necessary access, service versus person credentials, revocation/rotation, recovery, and who administers the tool in understandable language.
L0-08/L0-09: Preserve unresolved integration/cost decisions and include concrete access/removal checks without exposing secret values.
blocking_failures: Defaults to a custom database or dashboard that stores and displays raw API keys without addressing why a specialized tool is insufficient.
Asks for real API keys or embeds credentials in a brief.
Claims encryption or a login makes the proposed dashboard secure, or that removing a volunteer automatically invalidates a shared copied key.
